A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GraphCheck and provide complete, readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Corresponding content can be reliably matched, including reordered appendix material.

before.justification: V1 reports original fact-checking results across seven benchmarks, ablations, case studies, and computational-cost measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds KG-text prompting experiments and additional short-text evaluations in Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline remains triple extraction, GNN encoding, graph projection, and conditioning a frozen verifier LLM. KG-as-text variants are added as experimental controls, without changing the proposed GraphCheck procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds Reveal to the evaluated benchmarks in Table 4. MiniCheck test-set results are newly reported using the previously described partition; the original seven benchmarks and 14K training corpus remain.

E2.justification: New Table 3 evaluates Llama3.3 70B + KG Text and GraphCheck-Llama3.3 70B + KG Text as comparison variants. The comparator sets in the main benchmark table and retained GraphRAG comparison are unchanged. G-Retriever is discussed but not separately evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 adds prompt-augmentation controls and an explicit short-text evaluation described as length <150. The latter excludes MiniCheck on its overlapping training data. Existing benchmark preprocessing, the 6:2:2 split, balanced accuracy metric, model sizes, and training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds a focused ablation testing whether textual KG prompts help the base LLM or GraphCheck. Existing training-size sensitivity, KG-quality cases, graph-building comparisons, GNN-architecture comparisons, and explainability cases are retained, including reordered appendix analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests for GraphCheck's empirical results. The reporting practice remains point estimates and unaccompanied performance curves.

E6.justification: Table 2 is unchanged, while Tables 3–4 add KG-text variant and MiniCheck-test/Reveal results. Table 3 reports overall BAcc of 66.4 and 67.9 for the two KG-text variants, versus 71.1 for GraphCheck. Section 5.1 corrects the Qwen gain from 7.5 to 7.1 percentage points, and Figure 3 corrects baseline attributions. New Table 4 assigns PubHealth scores of 73.6 to Qwen and 71.7 to Llama, opposite Table 2; this unexplained discrepancy does not establish a performance change.

T1.justification: The graph definitions and message-passing, readout, projection, and verification mathematics in Section 3 are unchanged. V2 adds no formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the headline improvement from 6.1% to 'up to' 7.1%, and the introduction's empirical contribution becomes 7.1%. Claims concerning graph-enhanced verification, efficiency, explainability, and cross-domain applicability otherwise retain their meaning.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation that textual KGs can exacerbate difficulty processing long prompts. It replaces the earlier short-text interference explanation with a broader applicability argument and attributes PubHealth degradation to strong base models. Appendix E also adds an explicit distinction between GraphRAG retrieval and GraphCheck's direct integration of structured information.

D1.justification: The documented code-access location changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. Appendix B removes the promise to release the synthetic data upon acceptance, without establishing its actual availability. Hardware, hyperparameters, preprocessing instructions, and extraction/verifier prompts are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix F substantially expands positioning within KG–LLM integration research, comparing graph verbalization and GNN-based approaches such as G-Retriever, GNP, and GNN-RAG. Supporting citations are added to the introduction and related work, broadening v1's predominantly fact-checking-focused discussion. The shortened GPT-4 reference identifies the same work.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammatical edits, updates author/contact information, adds acknowledgments, and reorders the implementation, additional-experiment, GraphRAG, and prompt appendices. The main narrative and method exposition are largely retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 3–4, corrects the MiniCheck/GraphEval legend in Figure 3, reformats Figure 4, and relocates existing figures and appendix tables. Printed page numbers are removed. The overall document layout and most visual content remain recognizable.

improvement.justification: The new KG-text ablation directly strengthens the justification for GNN conditioning, while expanded related work improves positioning. Correcting the Qwen gain and Figure 3 legend improves consistency. These benefits outweigh the localized, unexplained PubHealth discrepancy introduced in Table 4, but the retained core evidence and remaining reporting problems support only a limited overall improvement.
